context: Fix the credential, catalog and endpoint facts the OpenCode Go verticals will be built on: Keychain-backed key resolution with a read-only OCGO_API_KEY alias, catalog discovery with a bounded offline fallback, measured endpoint selection, and a committed bare-exposure artifact with a fail-closed --check.
root_causes: The planned per-model protocol split was inherited from ocgo's hand-maintained 16-entry UsesAnthropicEndpoint table, which was never verified against the 29 live ids.
The OpenCode Go key reaches the process through the environment, which every spawned CLI inherits wholesale, so exposure is a property of the launcher rather than of the adapter.

Which catalog ids are bare-exposable is derived from the live routing index, so it changes whenever any other backend gains a model, with no signal that a user's saved model string now resolves elsewhere.
evidence: Measured 2026-08-22 on all 29 catalog ids against both upstreams: 22 returned 200 on both /messages and /chat/completions; only grok-4.5 refused the Anthropic format ('Model grok-4.5 is not supported for format anthropic').
ocgo forces minimax-m3, minimax-m2.7, minimax-m2.5 and qwen3.7-max onto /messages; all four answer /chat/completions, so its table is wrong in substance and not merely stale.

A first measurement pass sending string-form content produced 15 spurious 400s that read as endpoint rejections; the upstream errors ('messages must not be empty') showed the gateway was dropping the body, and block-form content returned 200 for all 15.
/messages returns AuthError 'Missing API key' for an Authorization: Bearer header and accepts only X-API-Key, while /chat/completions requires the bearer form.
The edge returns Cloudflare error 1010 to a default client fingerprint, so a User-Agent is required even on the public /models path.
Against the live routing index, 3 of 29 ids are already claimed (deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-pro by deepseek, kimi-k3 by kimi), leaving 26 bare-exposable.
solutions: Resolve the key from OPENCODE_API_KEY first and OCGO_API_KEY second, treating blank or whitespace as absent so an empty export cannot mask a working alias; never write the alias.
Add OPENCODE_API_KEY to the Keychain map and suppress the missing-key warning when the read-only alias is present, without promoting the alias into the canonical variable.
Scrub both names from every spawned CLI environment via LAUNCHER_SCRUB_ENV_KEYS.
Select the endpoint dual-protocol by default with a narrow declared deny-list of exactly the measured refusals, rather than encoding a 29-entry table of 22 identical rows.
Commit the computed bare-exposure set as an artifact and police it with a fail-closed --check wired into the test suite so it gates rather than merely existing.
acceptance_criteria: OPENCODE_API_KEY wins over OCGO_API_KEY, and the alias is never written or promoted.
A blank canonical export falls through to a usable alias rather than masking it.
An absent credential raises rather than returning a partial key, and no error message echoes a key.
A pre-set key short-circuits the Keychain read so tests and CI inject directly.
A pre-set alias suppresses the missing-key warning, while a genuinely absent key still warns.
Both names are absent from the environment of every spawned CLI.
Catalog discovery parses the OpenAI list shape, skips unusable rows, and degrades to a bounded 29-id fallback offline.
Endpoint selection is dual-protocol by default; only measured refusals are denied, and every deny-list entry is a known catalog id.
The bare-exposure artifact partitions the catalog with no id dropped or double-counted.
--check fails closed on drift, on a missing artifact and on an unparseable artifact, and is proven falsifiable by injecting a collision.
verification: pytest --override-ini pythonpath=src tests/unit/test_opencode_credentials.py tests/unit/test_opencode_catalog.py tests/unit/test_opencode_exposure.py tests/unit/test_opencode_env_exposure.py tests/unit/test_docs_dash_clean.py -q
legacy_risk_reason: touches the proxy startup credential path and the launcher env scrub shared by every provider; a regression either leaks a subscription key into spawned CLIs or breaks credential injection for deepseek
